newsitem.title: USA: S&P AFFIRMS FORTIS BENEFITS INSURANCE CO RATINGS.
newsitem.headline: S&P AFFIRMS FORTIS BENEFITS INSURANCE CO RATINGS.

text.p: NEW YORK, Aug 6 - Standard & Poor's today has affirmed its double-A' claims-paying ability and issuer credit ratings of Fortis Benefits Insurance Co. (FBIC) and its First Fortis Life Insurance Co. subsidiary.
The rating reflects the company's strong market positions in its chosen niches, strong operating performance, excellent capitalization, superior liquidity, and quality investment portfolio.
These factors are offset by the uncertainty regarding its ultimate business position in its variable product segment.

Through Fortis Financial Group, FBIC is a growing writer of variable annuities and variable universal life products. First Fortis Life Insurance Co. 's rating is based on its strategic importance to FBIC as its New York-licensed operation.
MAJOR RATING FACTORS:
-- Excellent capitalization: FBIC's capitalization is considered excellent. Standard & Poor's capital adequacy ratio has increased slightly from 165% in 1994 to 169% as of year-end 1996.
The improvement comes from solid earnings and a sizable capital contribution ($60 million) from its parent, Time Insurance Co.

-- Superior liquidity: FBIC's superior liquidity is due primarily to the large proportion of its investment portfolio in highly liquid corporate and government bonds. Liquidity is also enhanced by the fact that almost 90% of FBIC's liabilities maintain either surrender charges or withdrawal restrictions.

-- Strong operating performance: FBIC's operating performance is strong, with GAAP return on assets of 1.82% in 1996 and return on revenues of 4.1%. GAAP earnings have improved through the first quarter of 1997, with a return on assets of 2.17% and return on revenues of 5.3%.
Standard & Poor's expects FBIC will continue to generate good profitability, with GAAP return on assets ranging between 1.8%-2.0% for 1997.
-- Conservative investment portfolio: FBIC's investments are largely in publicly traded corporate bonds and U.S. government securities.
As of year-end 1996, bonds represented 68.3% of invested assets. The average credit rating is single-A'-plus with only 5% of the portfolio below investment grade.
Mortgages represent about 19% of the portfolio and has experienced better-than-average performance, with problem mortgages representing only 0.3% of the portfolio.
-- Strong ultimate ownership: Fortis Inc. is owned by Fortis AMEV of the Netherlands and Fortis AG of Belgium.

Fortis Inc. receives the implicit support of its ultimate parent, as demonstrated by the shared name, participation of senior management on its board of directors, capital contributions, and loans to fund acquisitions.
-- Uncertain variable product business review: Fortis is investing in the variable annuity and variable universal life market.

The variable products business has yet to reach critical mass, and the distribution strategy in this business is continuing to evolve. Currently, Fortis Sales is the largest channel for its variable products.
EXPECTATIONS
-- GAAP return on assets to range between 1.8%-2.0%.
-- Pretax return on revenue to range between 5.0%-5.5%.
-- Capital adequacy ratio to remain around the current level. Wednesday, 6 August 1997 21:14:10 ENDS nN06299281
